mainTopic: Writing תפילין and spinning תכלת on חול המועד; how festivals affect mourning
overview: The amud opens with the last line of a משנה: on חול המועד a person may spin תכלת for his ציצית on his thigh. A ברייתא gives three views on writing תפילין and מזוזות on חול המועד. רבי מאיר allows it for yourself, or for others as a free favor. רבי יהודה allows a trick: sell your own and write new ones. רבי יוסי allows normal writing and selling, enough to make a living, and the הלכה follows him. A second ברייתא argues over whether תכלת may be spun with a stone or a spindle, and the הלכה allows both. A new משנה then teaches that a רגל cancels mourning that began before it: שבעה if the burial was three days before, שלשים if it was eight days before. It explains that שבת counts as a mourning day but does not interrupt mourning, while רגלים interrupt mourning but do not count. It then records a מחלוקת about whether עצרת, ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים act like שבת or like the רגלים. The גמרא ends with רב and רב ששת arguing whether the רגל cancels only the mourning restrictions or the days too, and shows one practical result: a mourner who did not cut his hair before the רגל may not cut it after.

steps.title: The משנה allows spinning תכלת on the thigh
steps.stepSummary: The last line of the משנה says a person may spin תכלת for his ציצית by rolling it on his thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a person may spin sky-blue wool for his ציצית on his thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה, which lists things you may do on חול המועד. It allows spinning תכלת for ציצית, done by hand on the thigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spinning on the thigh is a changed, less efficient way of working, not the usual method with a spinning tool. That change is what makes it acceptable on חול המועד. The גמרא will come back to this line later.

phrases.english: And one may spin on his thigh
sky-blue wool for his ritual fringes.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spinning תכלת for ציצית by hand on the thigh is permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: write for yourself, or for others as a favor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's view: you may write תפילין and מזוזות and spin תכלת for yourself, and for others only for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may write תפילין and מזוזות for himself and spin תכלת on his thigh for his ציצית. For others he may do it as a favor. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds detail to the משנה. The first opinion, רבי מאיר's, allows this work for yourself, and for other people only without payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's line is about money. Doing a מצוה item for your own use, or as a free favor, is fine. Doing it as a paid job on חול המועד is not.

keyTerms.meaning: the scrolls fixed to doorposts (plural of מזוזה)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
A person may write תפילין and מזוזות for himself,
and spin sky-blue wool on his thigh for his ציצית,
and for others, as a favor,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כּוֹתֵב אָדָם תְּפִילִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's ruling with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing תפילין and מזוזות is allowed for oneself, and for others only without pay.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: sell your own and write new ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows a trick: a person sells the ones he wrote for himself, then writes new ones for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He may use a trick. He sells his own, and then goes back and writes new ones for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a second opinion. He allows a way to earn money without openly writing for sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The writing itself is always 'for himself', so it stays permitted. Selling what he already has is a side result, not the reason he wrote. This lets him profit a little without openly working for pay.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: He may use a trick,
and sell his own,
and then go back and write new ones for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion that is more lenient than רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may sell his own תפילין and מזוזות and write new ones for himself.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: write and sell normally, enough for a living
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי allows writing and selling in the normal way, as much as needed to make a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: He may write and sell in his normal way, enough for his living.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives the most lenient opinion. A סופר may work as usual on חול המועד, as long as it is only enough to support himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No trick is needed. Open writing for sale is allowed. The only limit is amount: he may earn what he needs to live on, not build up extra profit.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כּוֹתֵב וּמוֹכֵר כְּדַרְכּוֹ
phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: He may write and sell in his usual way
as much as is enough for his livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כּוֹתֵב וּמוֹכֵר כְּדַרְכּוֹ כְּדֵי פַרְנָסָתוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may write and sell normally, up to what he needs for his livelihood.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב, or some say רבה בר בר חנה, ruled for רב חננאל that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ruled for רב חננאל, and some say it was רבה בר בר חנה who ruled for רב חננאל: The הלכה is that one may write and sell in his usual way, enough for his living.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the three opinions. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling repeats רבי יוסי's exact words, so the most lenient view is the practical one. There is a doubt about who gave the ruling, רב or רבה בר בר חנה. But the ruling itself is the same either way.

keyTerms.meaning: ruled for him (gave a practical ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, a סופר may write and sell תפילין and מזוזות normally, as much as he needs for his living, following רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rav ruled for Rav Chananel,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabba bar bar Chana who ruled for Rav Chananel:
The halacha is: he may write and sell in his usual way
as much as is enough for his livelihood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the three opinions of the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: one may write and sell normally, enough for a livelihood.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר and the חכמים on spinning with a stone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about spinning תכלת and brings a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר forbids using a stone; the חכמים allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may spin תכלת on his thigh.' The Rabbis taught: A person may spin תכלת on his thigh for his ציצית, but not with a stone. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: Even with a stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's line about spinning תכלת. It brings a ברייתא that argues over whether a simple tool may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows only bare-hand spinning on the thigh, because a stone makes the work easier and more like normal work. The חכמים allow a stone too, since it is still not the full, usual method.

keyTerms.meaning: stone (used as a simple spinning weight)

phrases.english: 'And one may spin sky-blue wool on his thigh.'
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: טוֹוֶה אָדָם עַל יְרֵיכוֹ תְּכֵלֶת לְצִיצִיתוֹ,
phrases.english: A person may spin sky-blue wool on his thigh for his ציצית,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא בְּאֶבֶן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: but not with a stone; these are the words of רבי אליעזר.
phrases.notes: A stone tied on as a weight works like a homemade spindle and makes spinning easier.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: Even with a stone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוֹוֶה עַל יְרֵיכוֹ תְּכֵלֶת. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's line about spinning and opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: spinning on the thigh only, not with a stone. חכמים: even with a stone.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: a stone yes, a spindle no
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports רבי אליעזר's view differently: a stone is allowed but not a spindle. The חכמים then allow both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in his name: With a stone, but not with a spindle. And the חכמים say: Both with a stone and with a spindle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different report of what רבי אליעזר held. In this version the whole מחלוקת moves one step more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי אליעזר forbids a stone. In רבי יהודה's version, he allows a stone and forbids only a real spindle. The חכמים in this version allow even a spindle.

keyTerms.meaning: a spindle, the regular spinning tool

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different reports of the same מחלוקת. Do not mix them up. In the first, the argument is about a stone. In רבי יהודה's version, a stone is agreed to be fine and the argument is about a spindle.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says in his name:
phrases.notes: 'His name' means רבי אליעזר, from the step before.

phrases.english: With a stone, but not with a spindle,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בֵּין בְּאֶבֶן בֵּין בְּפֶלֶךְ.
phrases.english: and the Sages say: Both with a stone and with a spindle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of the מחלוקת in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's report: רבי אליעזר allows a stone but not a spindle, and the חכמים allow both.

steps.title: The הלכה: spinning is allowed with a stone or a spindle
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, and רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן, rule that spinning תכלת on חול המועד is allowed with either a stone or a spindle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two chains of אמוראים both say: the הלכה is that one may spin, whether with a stone or with a spindle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the argument from steps 6 and 7 about spinning תכלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 רבי אליעזר forbade a stone, and in step 7 he forbade a spindle. The ruling goes with the most lenient view and allows both tools. Two separate chains of teachers report the same ruling, which makes it stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A stone, used as a simple spinning weight
A spindle, the normal spinning tool
And likewise said. Introduces a second teacher who says the same thing

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: and likewise Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halacha is: both with a stone and with a spindle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument in steps 6 and 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Spinning תכלת on חול המועד is allowed with either a stone or a spindle.

steps.title: The הלכה: write normally and sell for a living
steps.stepSummary: The same teachers rule that a person may write תפילין and מזוזות on חול המועד in the normal way and sell enough to support himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: he writes in his normal way and sells enough for his living.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats, with these teachers, the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי about writing on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 already ruled like רבי יוסי. Here a second set of teachers confirms it. No trick like רבי יהודה's from step 3 is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as he needs to make a living

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, spinning תכלת is allowed with any tool. Writing and selling תפילין and מזוזות is allowed normally, as much as needed for a living (like רבי יוסי).

phrases.english: And the halacha is: he writes in his usual way
phrases.notes: He means writing תפילין and מזוזות, the topic of steps 2 to 5.

phrases.english: and sells enough for his livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלָכָה: כּוֹתֵב כְּדַרְכּוֹ וּמוֹכֵר כְּדֵי פַרְנָסָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling from the same teachers, confirming step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: one may write normally and sell enough for a living.

steps.title: New משנה: a רגל cancels mourning that began before it
steps.stepSummary: If someone buried a relative three days before a רגל, the רגל cancels the rest of שבעה. If he buried eight days before, the רגל cancels the rest of שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who buries his dead three days before a רגל: the rule of seven days is canceled for him. If eight days before, the rule of thirty days is canceled for him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how a רגל affects mourning that already started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once mourning has begun before the רגל, the רגל wipes out what is left of that mourning period. Burying three days early cancels the rest of שבעה. Burying eight days early, after שבעה is done, cancels the rest of שלשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה
A pilgrimage festival: פסח, שבועות or סוכות
The rules of the seven-day mourning period (שבעה)
The rules of the thirty-day mourning period (שלשים)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who buries his dead relative
three days before a pilgrimage Festival —
the decree of seven days is canceled for him.
Eight days — the decree of thirty days is canceled for him.
phrases.notes: Read it as: if he buried eight days before the רגל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקּוֹבֵר אֶת מֵתוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים קוֹדֶם לָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: mourning and the רגל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רגל cancels the rest of a mourning period that began before it: שבעה if he buried three days before, שלשים if eight days before.

steps.title: The principle: שבת counts, רגלים interrupt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its ruling with a principle: שבת counts as a mourning day and does not interrupt mourning, while רגלים interrupt mourning and do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the חכמים said: שבת counts and does not interrupt. Festivals interrupt and do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason behind the ruling it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is counted as one of the mourning days, and mourning simply continues after it. A רגל is the opposite: it stops a mourning period that already began. But its days are not counted, so if mourning had not started yet, it must be done after the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: Counts toward the days of mourning

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. 'עולה' means the day is counted as part of mourning. 'מפסיק' means it cuts off the mourning period. שבת does the first only, and a רגל does the second only.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the basis for all the rules about how שבת and יום טוב affect mourning.

phrases.english: Because they said:
Shabbat counts, and does not interrupt.
Festivals interrupt, and do not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ: שַׁבָּת עוֹלָה, וְאֵינָהּ מַפְסֶקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת counts toward mourning but does not interrupt it. רגלים interrupt mourning but do not count.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: after the Temple, עצרת is like שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says that since the בית המקדש was destroyed, עצרת (שבועות) is treated like שבת for mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: from the time the בית המקדש was destroyed, עצרת is like שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds an exception for one רגל, שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the rule in step 11, every רגל interrupts mourning. רבי אליעזר says that today שבועות follows the שבת rule instead: it counts toward mourning and does not cancel it. He ties the change to the destruction of the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The name the חכמים use for שבועות
From the time it was destroyed

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From the time the Temple was destroyed,
Shavuot is like Shabbat.
phrases.notes: עצרת is the name the חכמים use for שבועות. 'Like שבת' means it counts toward mourning and does not cut it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, עֲצֶרֶת כַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view that treats one רגל (שבועות) differently from the general rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the Temple's destruction, שבועות is treated like שבת for mourning: it counts and does not interrupt.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are like the רגלים
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds that ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים cancel mourning, just like the רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are like the רגלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion. רבן גמליאל widens the group of days that cancel mourning to include ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 we learned that רגלים stop mourning, while שבת only counts as a mourning day. רבן גמליאל moves ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים into the 'רגלים' group. So they also cancel שבעה or שלשים.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, head of the סנהדרין

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are like the festivals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second תנא's opinion on which days cancel mourning, following רבי אליעזר in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים cancel mourning like the רגלים.

steps.title: The Sages reject both views
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say עצרת is like the other רגלים, while ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are like שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: not like this one and not like that one. Rather, עצרת is like the רגלים, and ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are like שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the חכמים, who disagree with both רבי אליעזר and רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against רבי אליעזר, the חכמים say שבועות still cancels mourning like the other רגלים. Against רבן גמליאל, they say ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים only count as mourning days, like שבת, and do not cancel mourning.

keyTerms.term: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה
keyTerms.meaning: Not like this one and not like that one

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. רבי אליעזר says עצרת is like שבת. רבן גמליאל says ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are like רגלים. חכמים say עצרת is a רגל, and ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים are like שבת.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה,
phrases.english: not like the words of this one and not like the words of that one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' and 'that one' are רבי אליעזר and רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: rather: Shavuot is like the festivals,
Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are like Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects both רבי אליעזר (step 12) and רבן גמליאל (step 13).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עצרת cancels mourning. ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים count as mourning days, like שבת.

steps.title: רב and רב הונא: the restrictions are cancelled, not the days
steps.stepSummary: רב and רבי הונא say a רגל cancels the mourning restrictions, but the mourning days themselves are not fully erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: the decrees are cancelled, the days are not cancelled. And so said רבי הונא: the decrees are cancelled, the days are not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It explains what the משנה meant when it said a רגל 'cancels' שבעה or שלשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב splits mourning into two parts: the restrictions (the 'decrees') and the count of days. The רגל removes the restrictions, but the mourning period still exists in some way. רבי הונא agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of the mourning period
An אמורא who agrees with רב

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying mourning goes on as usual after the רגל. The restrictions really are gone. Only the 'days' remain on the books, and step 18 shows a practical effect of this.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav said:
the decrees were cancelled,
the days were not cancelled,
And so said Rav Huna:
the decrees were cancelled,
the days were not cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: גְּזֵרוֹת בָּטְלוּ, יָמִים לֹא בָּטְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'cancels' from the משנה's rule in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רגל cancels the mourning restrictions, but not the mourning days themselves.

steps.title: רב ששת: even the days are cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds that the רגל wipes out the mourning days completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: even the days are also cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת disagrees with רב and רבי הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב ששת, nothing of the cancelled mourning period is left after the רגל. Both the restrictions and the days are gone.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
even the days were also cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ יָמִים נָמֵי בָּטְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב and רבי הונא in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רגל cancels both the restrictions and the mourning days.

steps.title: Why aren't the days cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason, and the practical result, of רב's view that the days remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the days are not cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רב's view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the restrictions are gone anyway, why does it matter that the 'days' remain? The גמרא wants to see what difference this makes in practice.

phrases.english: What is the reason the days were not cancelled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רב's view in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason and practical effect of saying the mourning days are not cancelled.

steps.title: If he didn't cut his hair before the festival, he may not after
steps.stepSummary: The days still count, so a mourner who skipped cutting his hair before the רגל may not cut it after the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if he did not cut his hair on ערב הרגל, he may not cut it after the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a practical case that shows the 'days' still matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רגל lifted the haircut ban, so he was allowed to cut his hair before the רגל. If he did not use that permission, the mourning days are still running. After the רגל the ban applies again, until the שלשים end.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב and רבי הונא, the רגל only gives a window of permission before it. If a mourner misses that window, the שלשים restrictions return after the רגל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical difference between רב and רב ששת. For רב ששת, the days are fully gone, so this mourner could cut his hair after the רגל.

phrases.english: For if he did not cut his hair on the eve of the festival,
he is forbidden to cut his hair after the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם לֹא גִּילַּח עֶרֶב הָרֶגֶל אָסוּר לְגַלֵּחַ אַחַר הָרֶגֶל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the days remain, a mourner who did not cut his hair before the רגל is still under the haircut ban after it.
